content.body:
The model five Spitfire had several combat improvements over earlier models, such as bigger guns, more protective armor and better all-around performance, plus, finally, the ability to utilize negative G maneuvers in combat.
While most noted for its combat record over the deserts of North Africa, the Mark Vb saw action in almost every theater of the war and was the basis for the Royal Navy's only carrier-based version, the Seafire.
Equipped with 20 mm cannons in place of half the previous .303 cal machine guns (leaving it with four still), this Spitfire was able to hit an enemy aircraft hard enough and quickly enough to really hurt it in the increasingly brief firing solutions that modern air combat was moving towards, as speed was emphasized over turn rate.
It was still the premier turn fighter in British Royal Air Force service in the European theater and one of the best of the whole of WWII. As the Spitfire evolved it became a more potent fighter and its adversaries were forced to keep up the pace, both by developing new designs and also by putting hard to find resources into the evolution of existing airframes in order to remain on an even par with the combat abilities of the famous Spitfire.
content.brief: TYPE: Fighter Interceptor MAX. SPEED: 587 km/h WEIGHT: 2,845 kg CREW: 1 ARMAMENT: 20 mm Hispano Cannons (2) .303 cal Browning LMGs (4)
content.title: Supermarine Spitfire Mk Vb
